battle.name: 狗稅戰爭
battle.theater: 紐西蘭北島霍基安加灣
battle.brief: 一八九〇年代，紐西蘭北島霍基安加區議會向每頭狗徵半克朗稅款，南霍基安加毛利人拒繳；一八九八年四月，普克米羅毛利人集結武裝，槍隊進逼拉韋恩，殖民地出動一百二十人、兩門野戰砲與兩挺速射砲；海上一八六二年式鐵甲早已退場，只剩皇家海軍單桅戰艦守住河口，最後靠議員斡旋收場。

kit.name: 鐵甲艦
kit.history: 木殼外面包了鐵。裝甲第一次比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。

countries: 交戰一方是紐西蘭殖民地，行動由霍基安加區議會主導：一八九〇年代區議會向轄內每一頭狗徵收兩先令六便士（即半克朗），並把登記收費交由委員委任的亨利·門齊斯逐村辦理；警務由奧克蘭總署派員執行，需要時可調北地民兵與皇家海軍作武力後盾，殖民地內閣與總督府在後方授權。另一方是北地霍基安加的毛利社群，核心是普克米羅的馬胡雷胡雷（Ngāti Māhurehure）一支，首領洪·里伊維·托伊亞以「匯聚」（Te Huihuinga）教團的名義領導，長老羅馬納·特·帕埃杭伊帶隊；他們自認脫離一八三五年的毛利議會運動（Te Kotahitanga），主張按《懷坦吉條約》保障的權利生活。地方白人社團、商人與農戶是這場衝突的背景陣營；整場對峙本質上是區議會與鄉村之間、帶著宗教合法性與槍枝的對抗。
countriesEn: One belligerent was the Colony of New Zealand, operating through the Hokianga County Council: in the 1890s the council levied a tax of two shillings and sixpence, a half crown, on every dog within the district, and handed the registration and collection to a man it appointed, Henry Menzies, who worked through the villages selling collars and tags; the police came from the Auckland constabulary, and the colonial government could call on the Northland militia, the volunteer force, and on the Royal Navy for coercive backing, with the cabinet and the governor's office authorising it all from behind. The other party was the Māori communities of the Hokianga in Northland, centred on the Ngāti Māhurehure people of Pukemiro, led by Hone Riiwi Toia in the name of the religious and political group Te Huihuinga, with the elder Romana te Paehangi heading the party that marched. They held that they had seceded from Te Kotahitanga, the Māori parliament movement founded in 1835, and claimed the right to live as Māori on the terms guaranteed by the Treaty of Waitangi. Local white settlers, traders and farmers formed the background against which the confrontation played out. The whole affair was, at heart, a rural struggle between a county council and a village, but one that carried religious legitimacy and rifles.
people: 洪·里伊維·托伊亞（Hone Riiwi Toia）是這場衝突的核心人物，既是「匯聚」（Te Huihuinga）教團的領袖，也被信眾視為先知；他早年受毛利王運動與「帕伊·馬里雷」（Pai Marire）一派影響，認定殖民法律正逐步吞噬毛利自治。一八九八年四月二十八日，他在普克米羅的 pa（村莊）召開集會，門齊斯與警員到場時，面前站著一百五十名武裝毛利人；長老羅馬納·特·帕埃杭伊（Romana te Paehangi）當眾表態，寧死不繳稅。稅務登記人亨利·門齊斯（Henry Menzies）於一八九七年六月獲區議會委任，一八九八年在普克米羅發出四十張傳票，並以押解往南方寒地監獄相威脅，嚇得部分人躲進樹林過夜。殖民地方面，陸軍中校斯圖亞特·紐奧爾（Stuart Newall）率領一百二十人的分遣隊登陸拉韋恩，皇家海軍「火炬」號（HMS Torch）則進駐河口。最關鍵的人是北地毛利選區議員洪·赫克·恩加普阿（Hōne Heke Ngāpua），他是 一八四五年豎旗者洪·赫克的姪孫，五月六日抵達後斡旋，換取托伊亞與同伴投降，使事件避開戒嚴與土地沒收。拉韋恩的牧師吉托斯（Gittos）與旅館老闆、承包商羅伯特·科克倫（Robert Cochrane）也在碼頭勸走武裝隊伍，化解了第一波衝突。
peopleEn: Hone Riiwi Toia was the central figure of the conflict, both leader and prophet of the Te Huihuinga group. He had been exposed to the Māori King Movement and to the Pai Marire current, and believed that colonial law was steadily consuming Māori autonomy. On 28 April 1898 he called a meeting at the pā, the village, at Pukemiro; when Menzies and the constables arrived, a hundred and fifty armed Māori men were standing before him, and the elder Romana te Paehangi declared in front of them that they would rather die than pay the tax. Henry Menzies, the registration officer for dogs, was appointed by the county council in June 1897; in 1898 he served forty summons at Pukemiro and threatened the people with removal to the freezing prison cells of the far south, which sent some of them to sleep in the bush. On the colonial side, Lieutenant Colonel Stuart Newall led a detachment of a hundred and twenty men ashore at Rawene, and the Royal Navy's sloop HMS Torch took station at the river mouth. The decisive figure was the Member of Parliament for Northern Māori, Hōne Heke Ngāpua, grand-nephew of Hōne Heke, the flag-salter of 1845; arriving on 6 May, he negotiated and secured Toia's surrender, sparing the district martial law and confiscation of land. In Rawene, the Reverend Gittos and Robert Cochrane, the hotelkeeper and contractor, talked the armed party down on the wharf and defused the first clash.
kits: 卡面上的鐵甲艦，代表的是一八六二年英國那一代「木殼外面包了鐵」的答案：HMS Warrior 同級的設計第一次令裝甲比砲更難對付，砲塔的設計從此繞著它轉。但必須講清楚：這一艘一八六二年的鐵甲並沒有出現在霍基安加灣，它在一八九八年早已退居後備；真正到場的是皇家海軍一八九四年的單桅戰艦「火炬」號（HMS Torch），鋼製船殼、單列縱帆，帶著艦砲與水兵，用來封住霍基安加河口，切斷海上的供應與人員進出。陸地上，殖民地分遣隊配備步槍、兩門野戰砲與兩挺速射砲；紐西蘭在一八九六年購入六挺 .577/450 馬丁尼·亨利式馬克沁機槍，架在野戰車架上，其中兩挺就用於這場戰爭。毛利一方既無砲亦無機槍，依靠前膛獵槍、少量舊式步槍與隨身刀矛。運輸方面，霍基安加內陸當時沒有鐵路，海上靠定期班船，陸上靠馬車與驛馬，政府部隊全部由海路登陸。
kitsEn: The ironclad on the card stands for the answer of 1862, the British school of the wooden hull wrapped in iron: designs in the line of HMS Warrior made armour harder to deal with than guns for the first time, and gun design had to turn around the armour from then on. It has to be said plainly, though, that this ironclad of 1862 never appeared in the Hokianga harbour; by 1898 it was long in reserve. What actually turned up was the Royal Navy's sloop HMS Torch of 1894, steel-hulled and single-masted, with guns and men, sent to seal the mouth of the Hokianga and cut the sea-borne supply and traffic. On land the colonial column carried rifles, two field guns and two rapid-fire guns; New Zealand bought six .577/450 Martini-Henry Maxim guns on field carriages in 1896, and two of them were used in this war. The Māori side had neither cannon nor machine gun, relying on percussion muzzleloaders, a few old service rifles and knives. On movement and supply, the Hokianga interior had no railway at the time: the sea route ran on scheduled steamers, the land route on coaches and packhorses, and the government force came ashore by sea.
tactics: 雙方打的都不是正規戰爭。毛利一方的戰術是「以民為盾、以槍為籌碼」：他們拒絕把槍枝集中登記，因為集中就等於交出談判的本錢；四月二十八日在普克米羅以集會方式表態，其後只派不足二十人的隊伍前往拉韋恩，故意在白天、公開沿大路進城，並事先放話不會傷及婦孺與定居者、開槍也只朝天，實際目的是用「出現」本身換取談判。他們分散住在內陸村落，靠樹蔭、山脊與河灣遮蔽，營地與殖民軍營地始終保持一段距離，避免被合圍，形勢不利就退入叢林。殖民地方面走的則是標準的殖民鎮壓程序：先以警務封鎖碼頭、登岸架設一門砲控制河口，再由一百二十人的武裝縱隊登陸拉韋恩，兩門野戰砲與兩挺速射砲隨隊後方，準備沿霍基安加河谷唯一的公路向瓦伊馬推進，把對方逼出來；海軍「火炬」號在河口巡弋，令對方無法以船隻補給。五月五日推進至山脊時，頭頂掠過兩發子彈，隊伍仍維持縱隊前進，隨後在瓦伊馬學校設營。
tacticsEn: Neither side fought a conventional battle. The Māori tactic was to use the people as a shield and the rifles as bargaining counters. They refused to have their guns registered in one place, because a register would hand over the very bargaining chip they held. On 28 April they made their statement in the form of a meeting at Pukemiro, and afterwards sent fewer than twenty men to Rawene, deliberately in daylight and openly along the main road, having said beforehand that no women, children or settlers would be harmed and that if they fired it would be into the air; the real purpose was to use their own appearance to buy negotiation. They lived scattered in inland villages, using tree cover, ridges and river bends for concealment, kept their camp a clear distance from the colonial camp so as not to be encircled, and withdrew into the bush if the situation turned against them. The colonial side followed a standard template for the suppression of unrest: first the police sealed the wharf and landed a gun to control the river mouth; then a column of a hundred and twenty men came ashore at Rawene, with two field guns and two rapid-fire guns in tow, ready to push along the only road through the Hokianga valley towards Waima and force the other side out into the open, while HMS Torch patrolled the river mouth so that nothing could be supplied by boat. On 5 May, as the column crested the ridge, two shots passed overhead; the troops marched on in formation and then pitched camp at Waima School.
data: 有據可查的數字都是小數，但足以刻畫對峙的規模。稅額方面，每頭狗兩先令六便士，即半克朗；門齊斯每賣出一條狗牌只抽成一先令，佣金極低，卻足以令他要逐村上門。一八九七年六月區議會委任門齊斯負責登記，一八九八年在普克米羅的 pa 發出四十張傳票。四月二十八日普克米羅集會，毛利方面出席一百五十人；其後真正前往拉韋恩者不足二十人，警方一方只是一名警長加五名警員，從奧克蘭乘船抵達，並在碼頭架起一門砲。殖民地主力是一百二十人，配步槍、兩門野戰砲與兩挺速射砲，由中校紐奧爾指揮，另有皇家海軍「火炬」號在海上增援。五月五日雙方各開兩槍之後，五月六日托伊亞與另外四人被捕，其後再拘十一人；托伊亞等五人被合共判處兩年半苦役，其餘被告罰款連訟費，後來獲得豁免。一八九九年三月十五日，獄方在預告的期限之後宣布提早釋放。一八九〇這個年份來自戰爭列表，指的是狗稅開徵與加重的年代；真正有槍有砲的對峙，發生在一八九八年四月二十八日至五月六日之間。
dataEn: The documented figures are small ones, but they are enough to fix the scale of the confrontation. On taxation: two shillings and sixpence a dog, a half crown; Menzies took only a shilling on every collar he sold, a commission so small that he still had to go door to door. In June 1897 the county council appointed Menzies to run the registration, and in 1898 he served forty summons at the pā at Pukemiro. At the Pukemiro meeting of 28 April a hundred and fifty Māori attended; fewer than twenty actually went to Rawene. The police side was one inspector and five constables, brought by sea from Auckland, who set up a cannon on the wharf. The colonial main force was a hundred and twenty men with rifles, two field guns and two rapid-fire guns under Lieutenant Colonel Newall, with the Royal Navy's sloop HMS Torch reinforcing from the sea. After two shots each on 5 May, Toia and four others were arrested on 6 May and eleven more were taken later; Toia and four others were sentenced to two and a half years' hard labour between them, and the remaining defendants were fined with costs, later remitted. On 15 March 1899 the prison authorities announced the prisoners' early release. The year 1890 comes from the war list and marks the decade in which the dog tax was imposed and tightened; the confrontation with actual rifles and cannon took place between 28 April and 6 May 1898.
cause: 直接起因是一筆新稅。歐洲人自一八五〇年代引入兔子，毛利耕地與糧食苗圃受害甚重，政府為滅兔而向每頭狗徵稅，理由是狗是獵兔的主力；一八九〇年代霍基安加區議會把稅率定在半克朗，連一般毛利家庭都難以負擔，遑論靠養狗獵兔維生的家庭。除此之外，這群人對殖民地法律的不滿也累積多年：公路五英里內的國有地要繳土地稅、車輛輪寬有限就要繳車輪稅、獵捕原生鳥類受季節限制，傳統採集權利逐步被收窄。宗教層面上，「匯聚」教團認為這些都是自治被侵蝕的表現，他們自認已脫離一八三五年的毛利議會運動，主張「不受干擾地做毛利人」，而托伊亞在集會上的預言——「如果狗都要抽稅，之後就輪到人」——正正把稅務問題升級成「下一步是抽人」的集體預警，令一場普通的催稅變成以武裝維護《懷坦吉條約》權利的集體抗命。
causeEn: The immediate cause was a new tax. Europeans brought rabbits into the country from the 1850s, and Māori gardens and food plots suffered badly; the government, wanting the rabbits destroyed, taxed every dog, on the ground that dogs were the main rabbit hunters. In the 1890s the Hokianga County Council fixed the rate at half a crown, a sum already hard for ordinary Māori households and worse for families who lived by hunting rabbits with dogs. On top of that, this group had been nursing grievances against colonial law for years: Crown land within five miles of a public road carried a land tax, vehicles with a given tyre width were taxed, and the taking of native birds was restricted by season, so that traditional gathering rights were narrowed step by step. Religiously, the Te Huihuinga group read all of this as encroachment upon autonomy; they held that they had seceded from the Māori parliament movement of 1835 and that they should be left to live as Māori. Toia's prophecy at the meeting, that if dogs were taxed then men would be next, lifted a tax dispute into a collective warning that the next levy would fall on people themselves, and what began as ordinary collection became a collective act of armed resistance to the rights guaranteed by the Treaty of Waitangi.
impact: 這場衝突最大的後果不在戰場，而在司法定性：托伊亞等人被控「意圖以武力起兵，迫使女王改變措施，並以武力阻止徵收稅款」，一場稅務爭議被用叛國框架處理，判囚兩年半苦役。更深一層，恩加普阿事前拍電報勸托伊亞解散並改為請願，並非出於軟弱，而是他清楚知道前例：一八六三年《鎮壓叛亂法》一旦生效就會停止人身保護令、宣布戒嚴，《新西蘭定居法》更可以沒收「叛亂毛利人」的土地，這場戰爭幾乎把北地拉回一八六〇年代的鎮壓劇本。另一方面，選區議員介入、酋長請願、囚徒提前獲釋，證明一條不靠槍的路行得通，這一點對其後的毛利政治與土地政策走向影響深遠。制度上，狗稅照舊徵收，霍基安加的這筆稅一直留存到今日，也一直近乎無人理會：抗爭沒有改變稅制，但改變了「用甚麼方式爭取」的答案。
impactEn: The largest consequence of this confrontation was not to be found on the ground but in the way the law treated it. Toia and the others were charged with conspiring to levy war on the Queen in order to force her to change her measures, and with conspiring by force to prevent the collection of taxes: a tax dispute handled with the framework of treason, and sentences running to two and a half years' hard labour. Deeper still, Ngāpua's earlier telegram urging Toia to disband and to petition instead of fight was not weakness but calculation, for he knew the precedent. Had the Suppression of Rebellion Act of 1863 been triggered, habeas corpus would have been suspended and martial law declared, and the New Zealand Settlements Act would have allowed the land of rebel natives to be confiscated; this war came close to dragging the Northland back into the script of the 1860s. In the other direction, the intervention of a member of parliament, the petitions of chiefs and the early release of the prisoners showed that a route not dependent on firearms could work, and that point weighed heavily on the direction of later Māori politics and land policy. Institutionally the dog tax went on being collected: the Hokianga tax is still in being today, and still largely ignored. The protest changed no tax; what it changed was the answer to the question of how one is to fight for what one is owed.
result: 結果是不流血收場。五月六日，恩加普阿與托伊亞達成停戰，托伊亞交出部分槍枝，與同伴一起投降，五人當場被捕，其後再拘十一人，被捕者包括另外三位首領；毛利的武裝隊伍則解散返回內陸村落。法庭以「意圖起兵迫使女王改變措施、以武力阻止徵稅」定罪，托伊亞與另外四人合共判處兩年半苦役，其餘被告罰款連訟費，後來獲得豁免。一八九九年三月十五日，托伊亞在服刑期間獲提前釋放，據記錄多由霍基安加與北地各部族共同請願所致。出戰的毛利一方全程只開過兩發槍，殖民地部隊亦沒有開火，雙方都沒有戰死記錄，所以後世形容它是一場「沒有流過血的戰爭」。它也被視為十九世紀紐西蘭毛利戰爭的最後一聲餘響：武力沒有換到撤稅，但換到了一個新的做法——由酋長與議員帶頭，用請願、陳情與選舉去爭取應有的權利。
resultEn: It ended without blood. On 6 May Ngāpua and Toia came to terms: Toia gave up some of his rifles and surrendered with his people; five were arrested on the spot and eleven more were taken later, among them three other leaders, while the Māori war party dispersed back to the inland villages. The court convicted them of conspiring to levy war against the Queen so as to change her measures, and of conspiring by force to prevent the collection of taxes; Toia and four others were sentenced to two and a half years' hard labour between them, and the remainder were fined with costs, later remitted. On 15 March 1899 Toia was released before his sentence had run, which the record attributes largely to petitions from the iwi of the Hokianga and the far north. The Māori side fired two shots in the whole business and the colonial troops never fired at all; there are no battle deaths on either side, which is why later accounts call it a war in which not a drop of blood was shed. It is also regarded as the last echo of the nineteenth-century New Zealand wars: force won no repeal of the tax, but it did produce a new method, with chiefs and members of parliament leading the way and claims pursued by petition, by parliamentary motion and at the ballot box rather than by gunfire.
